<objective>
Widen the proven registry slice from add/list to the full lifecycle a human actually needs: show a project with its live `.fleet.yml`, update its metadata, and remove it non-destructively — each one a complete vertical slice from CLI flag through HTTP route through registry through SQLite, with CLI/HTTP parity machine-checked rather than maintained by hand.

Purpose: Phase 1 success criterion 1 requires register, list, update AND remove over both surfaces. Plan 01's tracer proved the path; this plan builds out from it without changing its shape.
Output: `fleet project show|update|remove` working over both CLI and HTTP, `.fleet.yml` read live and validated, and a parity test that fails if a subcommand ever stops mapping 1:1 onto a route.
</objective>

<user_story>
**As a** solo developer,
**I want to** inspect, retag, and retire a registered project from the terminal without ever risking the repo itself,
**so that** my registry stays accurate over months of use and a mis-typed removal can never cost me history or source.
</user_story>

  <name>Task 1: Live `.fleet.yml` read with safe parsing and warn-not-block validation</name>
  <read_first>
    - .planning/phases/01-foundation-registry-state-machine/01-CONTEXT.md D-17 (live re-read, zod, warn not block) and the PROJ-05 line in .planning/REQUIREMENTS.md

  </read_first>
  <files>src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts, src/registry/fleet-yaml.test.ts</files>
  <behavior>
    - A repo with no `.fleet.yml` yields `{ present: false, config: null, warnings: [] }`.
    - A repo with a valid `.fleet.yml` yields `{ present: true, config: {...}, warnings: [] }` with fields typed by the zod schema.
    - Editing the file on disk and calling `readFleetYml` again yields the new value — nothing is cached across calls.
    - A file that is not parseable YAML yields `{ present: true, config: null, warnings: [<message naming the parse failure>] }` and does not throw.
    - A file that parses but fails the zod schema (for example `setup` given as a string instead of an array) yields `config: null` and a warning naming the failing path.
    - An empty file, a comments-only file, and a file whose document is `null` all yield `{ present: true, config: {}, warnings: [] }`.
    - A file whose first bytes are a UTF-8 byte-order mark parses identically to the same file without one.
    - A file containing a YAML alias or a custom tag does not cause any code to execute; it is either parsed as inert data or reported as a warning.
  </behavior>
  <action>
Write the tests in `src/registry/fleet-yaml.test.ts` first, one per `<behavior>` bullet, backed by real temp directories, and confirm they fail before implementing.

`src/registry/fleet-yaml.ts` exports `FLEET_YML_FILENAME = '.fleet.yml'`, the zod schema `fleetYmlSchema`, and `readFleetYml(repoPath)`.

The zod schema covers exactly the four fields PROJ-05 names, all optional: `setup` as an array of strings, `test` as a string, `env_profile` as a string, `protected_paths` as an array of strings. Use a strict object so an unknown top-level key becomes a warning rather than being silently ignored — an unrecognized key in a config file the user believes is taking effect is exactly the kind of silent divergence D-17 exists to prevent.

Parse with the `yaml` package's `parse` function, which uses a safe schema by default and does not construct arbitrary types or execute anything at parse time. Do not use a loader variant that accepts custom types.

`readFleetYml` is total: it never throws to its caller. Read the file with `fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8')`; treat `ENOENT` as `present: false`; strip a leading byte-order mark before parsing; catch a parse failure and return it as a warning string; run the parsed value through `fleetYmlSchema.safeParse` and, on failure, return `config: null` plus one warning per zod issue naming its `path` and `message`. A YAML document that parses to `null` or `undefined` (empty file, comments only) normalizes to `{}` with no warning.

The function re-reads from disk on every call and holds no module-level cache. That is D-17's entire point: the file lives inside a repo that changes with commits, so a snapshot would go stale silently.

Do not implement, invoke, or shell out to anything from the `setup` or `test` fields. Phase 1 reads and displays them; acting on `setup` is Phase 2 (WT-05) and re-verifying `protected_paths` against a diff is Phase 4 (SAFE-09).
  </action>
  <verify>

  <action>
Write the integration tests in `src/registry/registry.test.ts` first — using Fastify's `inject()` against a real temp `FLEET_HOME`, no network — one per `<behavior>` bullet, and confirm they fail before implementing.

Extend `src/registry/projects.ts` with four functions alongside the existing `createProject`/`listProjects`. `getProject(db, idOrSlug)` resolves by exact id match first then exact slug match, and throws the typed `not_found` error when neither matches. `updateProject(db, idOrSlug, patch)` accepts only `name`, `envProfile`, `notes` and `tags`, writes them through Drizzle's parameterized update, and returns the full updated row; a patch touching any other column is a caller error, not a silent no-op. `archiveProject(db, idOrSlug)` sets `archived_at` to the current ISO-8601 UTC timestamp only when it is currently null, and returns the row either way, so repeating the call converges rather than moving the timestamp. `purgeProject(db, idOrSlug)` first selects tasks for the project whose `status` is not in the terminal set `done`, `failed`, `rejected`; if any row comes back it throws the typed `purge_refused` error carrying the offending task ids in `details`; otherwise it deletes the project row inside a single Drizzle transaction. No function in this module reads, writes, or stats anything under `repo_path` — removal never touches the underlying repository, per PROJ-04.

Add `purge_refused` to `src/api/http/errors.ts` mapped to HTTP 409, and `not_found` to 404 if Plan 01 did not already map it.

Extend `src/api/http/routes/projects.ts` with `GET /projects/:idOrSlug` (zod params of `{ idOrSlug: string }`; the handler calls `getProject` and then `readFleetYml(project.repoPath)` on every request so the config is live per D-17, and merges the yml warnings into the response `warnings` array), `PATCH /projects/:idOrSlug` (zod body strictly limited to the four mutable fields so any other key fails validation before reaching the registry), and `DELETE /projects/:idOrSlug` (zod querystring `{ purge?: boolean }` selecting `archiveProject` or `purgeProject`).

Extend `src/cli/index.ts` with `fleet project show <idOrSlug> [--json]`, `fleet project update <idOrSlug> [--name] [--env-profile] [--notes] [--tags] [--json]` and `fleet project remove <idOrSlug> [--purge] [--json]`, each a single `apiRequest` call against the matching route and nothing else. `--tags` accepts a comma-separated list and is sent as a JSON array. `show` renders three sections through `render.ts`: the stored metadata table, the live `.fleet.yml` fields when present, and any warnings printed to stderr. Keep format selection driven purely by the explicit `--json` flag.

Extend `src/cli/render.ts` only as needed to render a key/value detail view alongside the existing row table; keep both formatters pure so `parity.test.ts` can call them without a daemon.
